result.summary:
PASS on all six acceptance criteria. Every figure below is real quoted output, not inferred.

ENVIRONMENT. `grep LETFLOW_DB_PORT .env` -> `LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5472`, confirmed before anything ran. `docker ps` shows container `letflow-2-postgres-1` up 22h (healthy) mapping `0.0.0.0:5472->5432/tcp`; the sibling workspace's DB is the separate `letflow-postgres-1` on 5462 and was never touched. No `docker compose up` was issued in this worktree deliberately: compose would derive a NEW project name from this worktree's directory (`agent-ae4ed266bc89ede16`) and start a second container rather than reuse the correct, already-healthy one. `git rev-parse HEAD` -> 491363b14ab9f481584ce0efdc2067458aabc606. Working tree clean apart from the pre-existing untracked `docs/issues/ISS-0227.yaml`. Nothing in lib/, test/ or docs was modified, no commit, push, branch, checkout, stash or reset was performed.

(1) FULL SUITE -- PASS. Command `TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 sh scripts/test_parallel.sh`. N was set explicitly rather than left to nproc: the script's own header records ISS-0219 (an nproc-derived N -- 16 on this host -- crashes every partition during ecto.create/ecto.migrate before any Result: line), and this project's prior full-suite reports (e.g. test/reports/report-20260822-WF02-REQ075-20260822.yaml) use TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 as the established value for this host. Verbatim output:
  test_parallel: N=4 (source: env override)
  test_parallel: pre-compiling MIX_ENV=test (single compile, before any partition launches)
  test_parallel: TEST_POOL_SIZE=22 (computed: N=4, max_connections=100, headroom=10)
  test_parallel: partition logs in /tmp/letflow_test_parallel.izrIzA
  test_parallel: TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP=tp3785307 (shared by all 4 partitions)
  partition 1: 320 tests, 0 properties, 0 failures, exit 0
  partition 2: 373 tests, 0 properties, 0 failures, exit 0
  partition 3: 377 tests, 1 property, 0 failures, exit 0
  partition 4: 476 tests, 4 properties, 0 failures, exit 0
  ---
  combined: 1546 tests, 5 properties, 0 failures (1551/1551 passed)
All four partitions produced a Result: line and each exited 0, so the script's authoritative signal (parsed failure count) is 0. NOT AGENT ATTESTED CAVEAT: this invocation was piped to `tail`, so the script's own process exit code was consumed by the pipeline and is reported here as derived from its documented exit contract (exit 0 iff every partition has a Result: line and 0 parsed failures -- both hold), not as a directly measured number. The per-partition exit codes above ARE directly measured and are all 0.

(2) SCOPED PAIR -- PASS at 21 passed, exactly the expected figure. This needed two runs and the first one FAILED; the full diagnosis is below because it matters.
  First run, verbatim: `Finished in 37.4 seconds (0.00s async, 37.4s sync)` / `Result: 19/21 passed` / `Failed: 2 tests`, process exit 2.
  Second run, alone, verbatim: `Finished in 26.9 seconds (0.00s async, 26.9s sync)` / `Result: 21 passed`, process exit 0.
  The denominator is 21 in BOTH runs, which independently confirms RT-9 is collected: pre-change baseline for these two files was 20.

ATTRIBUTION OF THE FIRST RUN'S 2 FAILURES -- NOT ISS-0227. Established by evidence, not assumed:
  a. Both failures were in sandbox_pool_test.exs: `RT-7: a DB-free claim(0) is answered immediately while a provisioning is running` (:1035, asserting at :892 in its helper) and `RT-3 (death path a): a caller that dies while parked in waiting leaks no slot and no schema`. Both are the same assertion shape, `assert sandbox_schema_names() == baseline` -- a GLOBAL query over every `sandbox_%` schema in the database, not a query scoped to the pool under test.
  b. Before that run I checked `pg_stat_activity` and found a concurrent foreign `mix test` invocation connected to the same 5472 database (application_name `letflow_mixtest_27924`, 32 connections, backend_start 04:57:06Z; OS process erl.exe pid 27924 started 09:57 local and actively burning CPU). This is a shared host -- other agents run against the same database.
  c. The test output itself carries the smoking gun, verbatim from the run: `TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans/2: deferring this sweep entirely -- another mix test invocation (application_name != "letflow_mixtest_20168") is currently connected to this database, and this module tracks no per-row ownership, so an age-based reap right now could reclaim that invocation's still-live tenant schema (ISS-0110). Retrying on the next boundary sweep.` The reaper explicitly declined to clean up because of the sibling. That is the documented ISS-0110 guard behaving exactly as designed.
  d. I diffed the two MapSets in each failure rather than eyeballing them. RT-7: baseline 33 schemas, after-state 34 -- exactly one schema APPEARED (`sandbox_4d824c6d...`) that the test never provisioned. RT-3: baseline 35, after-state 34 -- exactly one schema VANISHED (`sandbox_36557117...`) that the test never released. Drift of +1 and -1 in OPPOSITE directions across two tests is the signature of a concurrent third party creating and dropping schemas in the shared database mid-assertion. It is not the signature of a leak. Note also that the baselines are 33-35 schemas rather than near-zero: the database was already carrying a large backlog of un-reaped orphans precisely because the reaper had been deferring.
  e. A real ISS-0227 regression would look categorically different. That change removed only write-only in-memory bookkeeping (owner_pid from the provision op, schema_name from the in_flight record) and a callerless helper; a genuine leak from it would show the pool's OWN schemas persisting after release -- appearing and never vanishing -- and would be deterministic, not +/-1 noise.
  f. DECISIVE: I waited for pg_stat_activity to report 0 `letflow_mixtest%` connections (polled to `conns=0`), then re-ran the identical command alone -> `Result: 21 passed`, exit 0. Reproducibly clean with the interference removed. This matches TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's prior finding on the same class of noise.
  g. Corroborating and arguably stronger: the full-suite run in item (1) already exercised the entire sandbox_pool_test.exs file, RT-7 and RT-3 included, and reported 0 failures across all four partitions -- and it ran during a window when no foreign mix test was connected (I polled and waited for that window before launching it).

No pre-existing non-SandboxPool failure was found anywhere, so no comparison run at 233af04 was necessary; the full suite is at 0 failures.

(3) mix compile --warnings-as-errors -- EXIT 0, measured directly (`echo $?` on an unpiped invocation, not inferred from absent output). Because a plain invocation on an already-built tree can be a silent no-op, I did not stop there: I re-ran as `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors`, which reported `Compiling 104 files (.ex)` / `Generated letflow app` and also exited 0. So the whole lib/ tree genuinely recompiled with zero warnings, not just an up-to-date short-circuit. This is step 3 of mix.exs's letflow.check alias and the merge gate at docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md:166.

(4) mix format --check-formatted -- EXIT 0, measured directly, no output.

HOUSEKEEPING. The temporary log files I redirected output into inside the worktree were deleted afterwards; final `git status --short` shows only `?? docs/issues/ISS-0227.yaml` (pre-existing) and `?? handoffs/WF03-ISS0227-20260822/step-06-test-runner.json` (this file). A `test/reports/` entry was initially withheld because this dispatch forbade modifying `test/`, which conflicted with TEST-RUNNER's role instruction to always write one; I flagged the conflict rather than silently resolving it. ISSUE-FIXER then confirmed the prohibition was a drafting error meaning test CODE only, and asked for the report. It is now written at `test/reports/report-20260822-WF03-ISS0227-20260822.yaml`, following the shape and filename convention of `test/reports/report-20260822-WF02-REQ075-20260822.yaml`, and it carries the full record including the failed-then-clean scoped run rather than only the clean figures. Nothing under `test/letflow/**` or `lib/` was touched. Final `git status --short` shows exactly three untracked paths: `docs/issues/ISS-0227.yaml` (pre-existing), this handoff, and that report.

issues.summary: First scoped-pair run returned 19/21 with 2 failures (RT-7, RT-3) caused by a concurrent foreign `mix test` invocation on the shared 5472 database, which made TenantSchemaReaper defer every sweep (ISS-0110 guard, logged verbatim in the run). Diffing showed +1 schema appeared in one test and -1 vanished in the other -- third-party drift, not a leak. Re-running alone after pg_stat_activity reported 0 mixtest connections gave a clean `Result: 21 passed`, exit 0. Not attributable to ISS-0227. No code change warranted.
